newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police track airport blackmail on Internet.
newsitem.headline: German police track airport blackmail on Internet.

text.p: German police scoured the Internet to catch a blackmailer who threatened to sabotage passenger aircraft with a remote-controlled model plane unless he was paid 50 million marks ($30 million), the Bild am Sonntag weekly reported on Sunday.

The blackmailer sent letters to 15 German airports threatening to steer a model aircraft into the jet turbines of an airliner as it was taking off, the paper said, and demanded that the German transport minister negotiate with him.
Federal investigators tracked the man down after he began communicating via electronic messages on the Internet computer network.
But by the time they caught up with the suspect, a 25-year-old computer freak with large debts, he was already in the custody of Hamburg police, who had detained him for alleged tax offences.
